lines.text: Chapter six, section one. Overview and objectives.
In the earlier chapters, our c-bettor always had a comfortable equity advantage, and that shaped every decision we made.
In real poker, the pre-flop aggressor often does not have an equity advantage on the flop.
This chapter is about c-betting when your range is not obviously ahead, and about defending when you are the caller who actually has the better hand.
You will find that the answer is not to c-bet less; it is to c-bet with a different shape of range and a different size.
Small bets that pushed equity in earlier chapters become risky here, because the caller can profitably raise them.
By the end of this chapter you should be able to identify boards where you have no range advantage and adjust your c-bet size and frequency accordingly.
You should be able to use pot control to preserve the equity of your medium hands rather than committing them to a big pot you cannot win.
You should be able to construct betting ranges on dynamic boards where hand values shift quickly.
And you should understand why sometimes the correct plan is to give up the initiative altogether and let the pre-flop caller do the work.
